Hi Anita — thanks for the questions. Below are concise, exportable answers. I attached a short summary PDF (redwood_data_handling_summary.pdf) and I copied Marissa (Product Security) and Ben (Solutions) for any implementation follow-ups.

1) Default storage locations (hosted API)
- By default, request/response payloads for the hosted API are stored in the region selected at account creation. For US accounts that is typically us-west-2, with replication as required for reliability inside the same cloud region family.
- Logs and observability metadata are stored in the same region where the workload is routed unless a customer elects cross-region replication.

2) Retention windows
- Ephemeral KV/prefix caches: default TTL is 1 hour (configurable per-tenant down to 10 minutes). These caches are in-memory on serving hosts and are flushed when instances are recycled.
- Request/response tokens (short-term request logs used for debugging/tracing): default retention is 30 days. Customers can request shorter retention (24h or 7d) or opt into zero-retention where we only keep ephemeral traces for the duration of the request.
- System logs / audit trails: default retention is 90 days for operational troubleshooting. Longer retention (custom retention windows) can be provided as part of Dedicated/Private offerings or on a contract addendum.

3) Deletion / erasure mechanics
- Customer-initiated erasure requests trigger a coordinated workflow: the account is flagged, active data stores are queued for deletion, and an erase job runs that removes tenant-scoped artifacts (request logs, caches, snapshots).
- Typical completion timeline for hosted API: 72 hours for primary deletion; additional 7–30 days to purge from cold backups depending on backup retention policies in effect at the time (we provide an estimated window in the erasure confirmation).
- Immutable backups: backups are on a 30–90 day rotation depending on system state; erase workflows mark data for omission from restores going forward and request removal at next backup cycle.
- We provide a deletion attestation upon completion (PDF) and an event in the audit trail with job id.

4) EU-only residency on Hosted API
- Yes — we support region-constrained hosting for accounts by routing and pinning all customer workloads and logs to EU regions (e.g., eu-west-1 or eu-central-1). This is enforced by account routing policies and smart routing rules that refuse cross-region fallbacks unless explicitly allowed in the tenant config.
- Evidence: we can provide region assignment screenshots, routing policy export, and an attestation letter. For regulated customers we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with geo-fencing for additional contractual guarantees.

5) Evidence & attachments
- Attached: redwood_data_handling_summary.pdf (summary of the above), and we can provide a SOC 2 report excerpt and an erase-playbook on request.

Notes / caveats:
- The hosted API allows customers to opt-in to additional logs/retention for debugging; opt-ins are recorded and can be revoked.
- For any legal hold requests, please loop Legal Ops and we will surface the retention suspension mechanism and the expected resume/purge timeline.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute call next week to walk GreenFrame's security team through the flow and provide the attestation.
